source.authoredBasis: Independent derivation from the complete written exercise: f={(x,2x+3):x>=0} is the closed ray starting at (0,3); swapping coordinates gives g={(x,(x-3)/2):x>=3}, a closed ray starting at (3,0), D_g=[3,+infinity), R_g=[0,+infinity). Candidate A is f: (0,3),(1,5),(3,9), closed start, upper-right arrow. Candidate C is g: (3,0),(5,1),(9,3), closed start, upper-right arrow. Candidate B deliberately removes the original restriction after swapping: the entire line y=(x-3)/2, through (-1,-2),(3,0),(9,3), with arrows in both directions, D=R=real numbers. Candidate D deliberately replaces x>=0 by x>0: the f-supporting ray with an open endpoint (0,3), so D=(0,+infinity), R=(3,+infinity). These are distinct deliberately authored alternatives, not source pixels. All panels have equal x/y unit length 24 pixels; A/B origins are (60,560)/(370,560), C/D origins (60,130)/(370,130) in the renderer's upward-y coordinates. Each panel displays x=-1..9 and y=-3..10; arrows indicate continuation beyond the drawn window, never finite domains. Light grids, axis labels, unit ticks, panel letters, visible (1,5)/(5,1) sample points and coordinate labels are explicitly modern schematic additions. A/C correspond by exchanging (0,3)<->(3,0), (1,5)<->(5,1) and all points on their rays.

notes: Independent authored-figure review retained at ssot-resources/soviet10year-textbooks/artifacts/8a/evidence/resume182-7-N36/choice-review-FIRST/review.json.record SHA ecc75c42bb9ea8bb62c63ec14955a1926fac4f38db3c281d58a566331a1feede. The disclosed draft basis and retained authoredBasis spec match the already-frozen actual pixels and written task 731: A preserves f's included (0,3) and slope 2; C preserves the converse's included (3,0) and slope 1/2. Swapping all pairs, not only sample points, yields the two correct rays. B deliberately drops the inherited restriction to make the whole inverse-supporting line, with both arrows and D=R=real numbers; D deliberately excludes input 0, producing the hollow (0,3), D>0 and R>3. Those are coherent intended wrong alternatives, not rendering defects. Spec SHA256 879c2909a2eb1b5be46fd442124776cb0fe72d053df747c94c7e257bef0dbcf3 fixes four 10-column by 13-row display grids with 24px x/y units and positive uniform aspect ratio. Its start/sample/tip positions agree with observed coordinates and slopes; A/C points correspond by coordinate exchange, B extends past (3,0) to the lower-left, and D's start is visibly open. Every panel title, axis label, zero, two unit labels and two point labels was visible in the previously opened complete image: all 32 labels, all solid rays/line arrows, and complete rightmost/bottommost ink. The retained render SHA256 12695264ee7fe779938ce7342650756ff7e8851b7fa2c5e0de64885248f0b9f3 binds this same spec and SVG at their persistent paths; it reports no collisions and minimum text 16px at the fixed 640px width. That report supplements, never replaces, the actual frozen visual inspection. No image, geometry or spec changed; no rerender or new opening occurred. The image gate approves the intentional candidates as drawn, not the mathematical truth of B or D as source answers.
